inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payment transactions' 189 (JPY millions); no separate equity-award tax line (SBC-zero market, 0.006% of revenue)
inputs.share_count_basis: Basic = diluted (no dilutive instruments; FY2025 diluted EPS shown as '-'). Dec-31-2025: 1,138,716,846 issued less 1,652,299 treasury = 1,137.06m; less ~11.1m shares repurchased Apr-Jun 2026 under the JPY30bn ToSTNeT-3 programme = ~1,126m at 30-Jun-2026 (estimate; the Q2 presentation does not print the count). The additional JPY40bn programme announced 4-Aug-2026 is not yet reflected and is value-neutral under the flat-count convention. Held FLAT.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-denominated build. 10y JGB ~1.8% (Nov-2026) + equity beta ~1.0 x Japan ERP ~6.0% = cost of equity ~7.8%; equipment-operations debt is small (JPY332bn vs JPY2.85tn market cap) at ~1% after tax, giving a mechanical WACC ~7.3%. Rounded UP to 8.0% as the house JPY large-cap industrial rate (house keiretsu-supplier reference is ~9%; Kubota is larger, more diversified and investment-grade). Management's own MTP2030 WACC is 5-6.5%, which we regard as too low. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariff and FX risk are charged in the scenario flows, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease payment (FY2025 principal JPY23,738m + lease interest JPY719m = JPY24.5bn, 0.81% of revenue) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (JPY83.3bn at Dec-2025) EXCLUDED from net debt (Kubota's 'Bonds and borrowings' already excludes them); D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A JPY130,476m less ROU depreciation JPY25,138m = JPY105.3bn, 3.49% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows: noncontrolling interests (Escorts Kubota and others; JPY245.5bn book at Jun-2026) took 13.9% of FY2025 profit (JPY30.1bn of JPY216.8bn), 11.3% in FY2024, 8.3% in FY2023, and received JPY42.7bn of cash dividends in FY2025. A 12% leakage is folded into cash_tax_rate_path: 1 - (1-0.27 cash tax)(1-0.12 NCI) = 35.8%, rounded to 36.0%. The NCI stock is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.captive_finance_treatment: Kubota consolidates a retail-finance arm (finance receivables JPY2,230.8bn, interest-bearing liabilities JPY1,924.9bn, equity JPY474.9bn at 30-Jun-2026 per the Q2 FY2026 presentation's Financial Services balance sheet). Its funding cost is booked in cost of sales (finance costs below operating profit are only JPY4.8bn), so consolidated operating profit / EBITDA already carries the finance arm's NET spread. The arm is therefore valued through the flows and its balance sheet is excluded from the bridge: net_debt is EQUIPMENT-OPERATIONS ONLY (interest-bearing liabilities JPY331.8bn less cash JPY229.1bn = JPY102.7bn). Deducting consolidated bonds and borrowings (JPY2,256.7bn) without the receivables would wipe ~JPY1,900/share of real value. Trade-off accepted: receivable-book growth is not charged as capital (management is shrinking the book; delinquency >90 days rose to 1.9% from 1.1%, which is in the bear case).
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer with trade receivables JPY1,002bn + inventories JPY689bn vs payables JPY296bn at Dec-2025 = 46% of revenue tied up; growth CONSUMES cash, so wc_capture is negative. Base -20% assumes the MTP2030 inventory (-30% months) and finance-term programmes offset roughly half the natural build; bull 0% (programmes fully offset growth); bear -40% (no offset, as in FY2021-23 when OCF went negative).
inputs.excluded_assets_memo: Bridge adds FVOCI equity securities (cross-shareholdings: Osaka Gas, SMTG, SMFG, Toho Gas etc.) at fair value JPY82.3bn and equity-method investments at JPY54.7bn book, because their dividend income (JPY2.3bn) and equity-method profit (JPY2.7bn) sit below operating profit and so are not in the flows. NOT added: time deposits JPY22.6bn, debt securities at amortised cost JPY70.7bn and FVTPL debt securities JPY81.0bn (JPY174bn, ~JPY155/share) because the FY2025 note does not split them between the finance arm and equipment operations; this is a conservative omission, flagged.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, cyclical non-US industrial; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 with owner-fcf-adaptations: JPY WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in flows, excluded-income matching assets, SBC-zero, captive finance excluded from bridge). First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). MID-CYCLE: FY2026 guidance (revenue JPY3,280bn, OP JPY400bn / 12.2%) includes an estimated JPY70bn one-off US tariff refund; underlying OP is JPY330bn (10.1%). Year 1 uses the guided peak; margins step back toward mid-cycle in year 2 and only partially re-climb toward the MTP2030 12% OP-margin target in base. FY2020-25 EBITDA margins ran 11.4-14.5% (mean ~13.6%). Buybacks: Kubota is a steady repurchaser (JPY20-50bn/yr), so the flat count is funded. DATA GAP: Q3 FY2026 results (due ~5-6 Nov 2026) are not in the folder; anchors are the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet and the 4-Aug-2026 guidance. Price is the regular Friday close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-horizon base revenue growth anchored on the 3-yr revenue CAGR (4.1%, FY2022-25) and the MTP2030 segment CAGRs (construction +8%, India +9%, lifecycle +7%, Japan ag flat-to-down); the 5-yr figures are inflated by the FY2021-23 yen-weakness and post-COVID restock surge
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-yr equity CAGR 11.7% vs revenue 4.1% diverges >30%: equity growth reflects retained earnings and yen-depreciation translation gains in OCI (77% overseas revenue), not operating growth. Not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2020 JPY54.0bn -> FY2025 JPY123.9bn (18.0% CAGR) vs reported 19.5%; the gap is interest income growing from JPY4.0bn to JPY17.9bn, not SBC (immaterial, JPY45-552m/yr). 3-yr FCF CAGR is undefined: FY2022 owner FCF was -JPY183bn (finance-receivable and inventory build). Reported FCF was negative FY2021-FY2023 and the MTP2030 itself notes negative cumulative 5-yr FCF over FY2021-25, so the FCF history is a poor growth anchor; revenue and margins are used instead.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Y1 = FY2026 guidance (OP JPY400bn + D&A ~JPY137bn = 16.4%) haircut to 16.2% for Q4 risk after the Sep-Oct sell-side downgrades. Y2 removes the JPY70bn tariff refund (-2.1pp) and assumes only a partial ag recovery: 14.3% = ~10.5% OP margin, the FY2023-24 level. Y3-5 climb to 15.0% EBITDA (~11.3% OP incl. ROU depreciation), i.e. the MTP2030 12% target is roughly 60% delivered. Held flat thereafter.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: 27% cash tax (FY2024-25 cash taxes 29%/31% of PBT on peak years; GAAP effective 24%; blended Japan 30.6%/US ~25%/India ~25%) plus 12% NCI leakage of post-tax profit = 36.0% combined. Not a statutory rate: see inputs.nci_treatment.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands near the raised guidance (revenue +8.6%, OP ~JPY395bn) with the JPY70bn tariff refund inside it. FY2027 is the reset year: the refund does not repeat, the yen is modestly stronger than the 157 assumed, North American compact tractors stay soft while construction machinery normalises from +36%, so revenue grows ~2% and EBITDA margin falls back to 14.3% (~10.5% OP, the FY2023-24 level). From FY2028 the ag cycle recovers (CNH's '2026 trough' thesis), India and lifecycle/parts compound at high single digits and the new CEO's price/incentive/fixed-cost programme lifts EBITDA margin to 15.0% by FY2030, about 60% of the way to the MTP2030 12% OP-margin target. Working capital: inventory and finance-term programmes offset half of the natural build. Terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF (Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x).
scenario_narratives.bull: Tariff refund is a bridge, not a one-off: structural US price increases stick, North American construction machinery keeps riding data-centre/power/housing capex, and the ag cycle turns up in 2027 rather than 2028. Escorts Kubota compounds at ~9% and becomes the low-cost export hub. The MTP2030 is delivered in full — 12% OP margin (16.2% EBITDA) by FY2030 — and inventory months fall 30%, so growth no longer consumes working capital (wc_capture 0). Cross-selling the installed base lifts parts/service mix. Still discounted at 8% and still capped at 15x: the bull is an earnings story, not a re-rating story.
scenario_narratives.bear: Peak-earnings extrapolation fails. Q4 FY2026 misses on a stronger yen and Middle East cost pressure (OP ~JPY375bn). In FY2027 the North American ag downturn deepens (low crop prices, 0-40hp residential demand hit by rates), US construction machinery gives back part of its +36% surge, Europe upland machinery restructuring charges land, USD/JPY moves to ~140, and revenue falls 5% with EBITDA margin back to 12.0% (~8% OP, below FY2025's 8.8%). The retail-finance book's >90-day delinquency (1.9% at Jun-2026, up from 1.1%) turns into credit losses; receivables and inventories keep absorbing cash (wc_capture -40%, as in FY2021-23). Recovery is slow: margin only regains the FY2025 13% EBITDA level by FY2030 and growth settles at 2%. Capital intensity stays higher (capex 5.3% vs 5.0%).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25%: FY2026 is a guided peak that contains a JPY70bn one-off, two major brokers downgraded in Sep-Oct 2026, ag peers call 2026 a trough with recovery unproven, 40% of revenue is one US demand pool exposed to tariff and rate policy, and the finance book's delinquency rate has nearly doubled. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs the MTP2030 margin target delivered in full under a brand-new CEO and governance structure, an early ag upturn, continued US construction strength AND a stable yen — several independent things. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kubota is valued as a cyclical industrial compounder on consolidated owner FCF, with the captive-finance arm valued through its net spread in operating profit and its balance sheet kept out of the bridge. FY2026 is treated as a tariff-refund-inflated peak, not a base: margins reset in year 2 and re-climb only partway to the MTP2030 target. Shareholders are charged for leases (treatment B), for the 12% minority leakage, and for the working capital that growth consumes; they are credited with the cross-shareholdings and equity-method stakes whose income sits below operating profit. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows, at a flat 8% JPY WACC; the terminal multiple is capped at 15x FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Peak-earnings extrapolation: FY2026 OP guidance of JPY400bn includes ~JPY70bn of one-off US tariff refunds; underlying is JPY330bn (10.1%)
North American ag equipment cycle (CNH: 2026 is the trough) and the 40% North America revenue concentration across tractors and construction machinery
FX translation: FY2026 guidance assumes USD/JPY 157 and EUR/JPY 183; yen appreciation of 10% would remove roughly JPY70-80bn of OP
Retail-finance credit: JPY2.2tn receivable book, >90-day delinquency up to 1.9% from 1.1% in six months; funding costs in cost of sales rise with US rates

Captive-finance bridge convention: valuing the arm through its spread and excluding its JPY475bn book equity is one of two defensible treatments; the alternative (strip the spread, add book equity) would move value by a few hundred yen per share either way
Working capital capture is the largest swing driver (-20% base vs 0% bull vs -40% bear); management's inventory and finance-term targets are unproven
Execution risk on the MTP2030 under a new CEO; European upland-machinery restructuring charges
Q3 FY2026 results (early Nov 2026) are not yet in the folder; the Y1 path should be re-checked against them
